title: Deutsch's Algorithm
summary: One query decides whether a one-bit f is constant or balanced.
mission: With a single call to oracle(qc), leave qubit 0 in |0⟩ if the secret one-bit function f is constant and in |1⟩ if it is balanced.

prediction.question: Suppose the auxiliary qubit is in |0⟩ (not |−⟩) and the input is in |+⟩ before the oracle. When you measure the input, what do you get?
options: Always 0 if f is constant, always 1 if it is balanced
0 or 1 with 50% each, whatever f is
prediction.explanation: The oracle produces (|0⟩|f(0)⟩ + |1⟩|f(1)⟩)/√2. The input becomes entangled with the auxiliary qubit and measuring it gives 0 or 1 with 50% each, for any f. Parallelism, without phase kickback and a final interference step, yields no information.

hints: Prepare the auxiliary qubit in |−⟩ with qc.x(1) and qc.h(1): then the oracle returns the phase (−1)^f(x) to the input.
Put qubit 0 in |+⟩ with a Hadamard before the oracle and apply a Hadamard to it again afterwards.
Sequence: qc.x(1), qc.h(1), qc.h(0), oracle(qc), qc.h(0).
